scenes.narration: Black holes are regions of space where gravity is so strong that nothing can escape — not matter, and not even light itself.
scenes.prompt: A dark sphere surrounded by a swirling accretion disk of glowing gas and dust in deep space, with distant stars visible behind it
scenes.motion_direction: Slow zoom into the black hole

scenes.narration: One way they form is when a massive star runs out of fuel and collapses under its own weight into an extremely dense core.
scenes.prompt: A dying red supergiant star collapsing inward, with visible shockwaves and a bright core shrinking
scenes.motion_direction: Pan left across the collapsing star

scenes.narration: The boundary where escape becomes impossible is the event horizon — the point of no return, where the black hole’s pull always wins.
scenes.prompt: A clear outline of a black sphere with a glowing ring around it, representing the event horizon
scenes.motion_direction: Zoom out to show more of the surrounding space

scenes.narration: Inside lies the singularity, a point of infinite density predicted by classical general relativity — where known physics breaks down.
scenes.prompt: A tiny, bright white dot at the center of a dark void, with faint gravitational lensing effects around it
scenes.motion_direction: Pan right to reveal more of the singularity's surroundings

scenes.narration: Near black holes, spacetime curves dramatically — bending light into arcs, distorting time, and warping space all around them.
scenes.prompt: A galaxy with a central supermassive black hole, light rays curving around it
scenes.motion_direction: Slow pan across the warped region

scenes.narration: Theoretical physics also predicts Hawking radiation — black holes may slowly evaporate over eons through faint quantum effects.
scenes.prompt: A black hole with faint, shimmering particles of energy escaping from its edge into space
scenes.motion_direction: Zoom out to show the whole scene and then fade
